name: Citation list
summary: Numbered sources on their own: title, publisher and date, a short excerpt where it helps, and a button to open each one.
use: to list the sources behind an answer, or reading to follow up on
states: button under the text on a phone
a11y: An ordered list, so each source is read with its number; every Open button is named with its source's title.

use_when: the person asks where an answer came from, or for sources or further reading on a topic
avoid_when: an answer with its sources: use answer-sources
files the person can download: use file-card
search results to choose from: use result-list

parts.name: title
parts.what: a heading for the list, such as Sources or Further reading

parts.name: publisher
parts.what: who published it, as plain text

parts.name: date
parts.what: when it was published or updated

parts.name: excerpt
parts.what: a short passage from the source that matters here

parts.name: open
parts.what: opens the source; the host decides where (no raw URL in the data)

empty.how: with no sources, say so in plain text instead of this part

loading.how: the renderer keeps two rows with muted blocks for title and publisher

error.how: a source that cannot be opened leaves out its open action

disabled.how: an item with no open action shows no button rather than a disabled one

overflow.how: up to ten rows stack; on a phone the button moves under the text

long_text.how: titles, publishers and excerpts wrap, and long words break

keyboard: Tab moves from one Open button to the next
